research_question: In adults with chronic neck pain, what is the effect of telerehabilitation delivering exercise or physical activity, compared with a minimal intervention (advice, educational materials, usual care without active rehabilitation, wait-list, or no active care), on pain intensity at short-term follow-up (>2 weeks to <=3 months)?
outcome_description: Self-reported pain intensity measured with validated instruments (such as the Visual Analogue Scale [VAS] or Numeric Rating Scale [NRS]) at short-term follow-up (between >2 weeks and <=3 months post-randomisation).
positive_direction: A positive effect size indicates higher pain intensity in the telerehabilitation group compared with the control group (worse outcome); a negative effect size indicates lower pain intensity favoring telerehabilitation (greater pain reduction).
search_queries: telehealth chronic neck pain physical activity controlled comparison
digital exercise chronic neck pain pain intensity outcome
inclusion_criteria: Empirical comparative studies or clinical trials involving adults with chronic neck pain
Evaluation of telerehabilitation delivering exercise or physical activity compared to minimal intervention (advice, education, wait-list, or usual care without active rehabilitation)
Reporting quantitative pain intensity data at short-term follow-up (greater than 2 weeks and no later than 3 months post-randomisation)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, study protocols, editorials, opinion pieces, or theoretical papers are excluded)

No isolated comparison between a telerehabilitation exercise arm and a minimal/no-intervention control condition (e.g., comparisons between two active rehabilitation arms or lack of isolated pairwise data)
No usable quantitative outcome data on pain intensity allowing effect size calculation, or study data internally contradictory with reported effect directions
Completely unrelated to adults with chronic neck pain or telerehabilitation exercise interventions
moderators_to_extract: Control group type (waitlist, usual care, education/advice)
Delivery modality (synchronous video, asynchronous digital/app-based, blended)
effect_size_note: Extract only isolated pairwise comparisons between telerehabilitation exercise and minimal intervention/usual care (excluding comparisons between two active arms and omnibus statistics). Select only one endpoint per study corresponding to short-term follow-up (>2 weeks to <=3 months). Do not extract outcomes other than pain intensity. Ensure reported direction of effect matches quantitative data.
